Neha / Marissa / Alice — draft attached (redwood_private_network_sketch_v1.png) plus short notes inline. High-level summary below; full slide attached to Drive (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-diagram).

Executive summary (2 lines):
- Redwood Private: control plane remains in Redwood-managed control plane; customer owns VPC and peering; inference nodes run in customer VPC or in dedicated tenant subnets depending on the package.
- Redwood Dedicated: reserved GPU pool per-customer with strict tenant fencing; control plane APIs remain Redwood-hosted but connections to the pool are authenticated and encrypted; egress via customer-managed NAT or Redwood-managed egress with IP allowlisting depending on contract.

Key diagram callouts (matching Alice’s asked bullets):
- Control/data plane: control plane (management APIs, model catalog) sits in Redwood control plane; data plane (inference traffic, model artifacts at runtime) resides in customer-dedicated subnets for Private or within tenant-isolated pools for Dedicated. Diagram labels: "Control Plane (Redwood)" vs "Data Plane (Customer/Dedicated)".
- Airlock/egress: we show an egress proxy (optional) and an outbound firewall cluster. For Private, customers can choose: (A) route outbound via their NAT/gateway (preferred for compliance) or (B) use Redwood egress with IP-allowlisted exit addresses.
- KMS: customer-managed KMS supported for encryption-at-rest of model artifacts and secrets; annotation shows keys never exported. Redwood KMS integration uses standard envelope encryption and HSM-backed CMEK options.
- Hardware/tenant fences: Dedicated pools use namespace isolation at the runtime and instance-level hypervisor isolation; physical GPUs are allocated to tenant pools and persistent volumes are segregated per-tenant. Diagram note: we do not publish hardware serials; we show logical separation only.

Open questions for Velora (short):
1) For Private, will Velora require Redwood-managed egress or do you prefer to manage NAT/peering yourself?
2) Any specific KMS vendor or HSM requirement we should call out?

Attachments: redwood_private_network_sketch_v1.png (attached here as a stub) and uploaded slide to Drive. I also created a short doc (redwood-enclave-cs-summary.docx) with the narrative and bulletized evidence pointers.
